_comment: HubSpot pipeline config for the daily-crm enrichment workflow — committed, no secrets. Rewritten 2026-08-19: this workflow is now enrichment-only. It adds context (notes + touch-tracking fields) to deals that already exist, and posts a stale-deal brief to Slack. It never moves a deal between stages, and creates a deal in exactly one case: a Shopify website contact-form enquiry with no existing deal (Lemlist replies already get a deal from a separate automation). Notion, Granola, HubSpot Task creation, Slack channel reading, and general deal creation were all removed in that rewrite. Updated 2026-08-20: Gmail lookback narrowed from 2 days to 24h (see sources.gmail), and a new pipeline-wide replyOwedAudit step added between the Gmail sweep and the Shopify check — see that block for why.

owners._note: Verified live against search_owners on 2026-08-19. A prior version of this file mislabelled 163314964 as 'Syb' — it is Alex. Syb Roell is 165632552 and owns no deals in this workflow. These two ids drive the step-4 Slack split.

_ownerPolicy_note: This workflow never sets and never clears hubspot_owner_id. Ownership is what the Slack stale brief splits on, so it is left exactly as found. (Superseded the 2026-08-18 rule that blanked the owner on every Reply-to-be-enriched deal — that rule would have emptied the very field the brief now groups by.)
_stages_note: Verified live against get_properties(deals, dealstage). Re-verify this way before trusting stage names — the board gets relabelled from time to time without this file being updated.
_neverMoveStages_note: ABSOLUTE. This workflow never writes dealstage — not on a positive reply, not on a confirmed call, not on a signed agreement, not on a clean decline. A decline gets Closed Lost SUGGESTED in the note and the digest; a soft 'not now' gets Interested (not now) suggested. Shaffy moves every deal by hand. If a run ever changes a stage, that is a bug and belongs in the digest.

enrichment._note: Step 1 sweeps every deal at sourceStageId and fills the fields below from the actual conversation (Lemlist full thread + every matching Front conversation + domain-wide Gmail + Calendly). Never derive a field from what HubSpot already stores — that stored value is what is being verified.

b2bType._note: Infer from what the practice actually is, per the reply or the company itself — not from the campaign name. Leave unset only if genuinely unclear.

enrichment._ordersPmDefault_note: Default to 1-5 only when the thread gives no volume signal. If a count is mentioned ('~250 TRT patients', '5-10/mo'), map it to the closest bucket: 1-5, 6-10, 11-25, 26-50, 51-100, 100-200.

declineHandling._note: Screen for this FIRST — a dead lead is not worth enriching. Clean decline: write the note explaining why it reads as a decline and SUGGEST Closed Lost in note + digest, then skip b2b_type/orders_pm/company backfill. Ambiguous (vague brush-off, deflection to a colleague): a [flag-uncertain] note and its own digest line. Never set a stage either way.

fieldRefresh._note: description and hs_next_step render on the HubSpot board cards, so both stay short. Refreshed whenever the workflow touches a deal.
fieldRefresh._nextStepFormat_note: A dated log, not prose — newest line first, no year, no leading zeros ('8/14' not '08/14'). PREPEND a new line on each touch; keep the 4 most recent. If a deal is touched twice in one day, replace that day's line rather than adding a second.

defaultACV._note: Every deal carries an amount so the board's weighted-pipeline total means something. Fill only when blank — never overwrite a real value.

notes._note: ONE note per email THREAD, holding the full thread, updated in place — rewritten 2026-08-19, replacing the old one-note-per-individual-message model. The identity line is the dedup key: search the deal's existing notes for it before writing. Match with current Latest: line => skip, change nothing (the common case on a re-run). Match with an older Latest: => UPDATE that note in place to carry the full current thread. No match => create. Never write a second note for a thread that already has one; separate threads on one deal each keep their own note.
notes.body: Full thread in chronological order, each message labelled with its date and sender.

touchTracking._note: Set every field below in ONE edit per deal, recomputed from a fresh full-thread read across Lemlist + Front + Gmail + Calendly. Never trust a stored value because 'nothing new happened today' — several have been wrong since the deal was created.

lastTouchDate._note: The true last message from ANY source, including a Calendly booking/acceptance. Never infer from hs_lastmodifieddate — unrelated property backfills touch that with no real contact.

lastTouchDirection._note: Inbound = the lead replied or booked/accepted a call. Outbound = we sent the last message and have not heard back.

lastMessage.calendarEventFormat: {Client|SwimScore}: accepted/sent the "{event name}" calendar invite for {date}
lastMessage._note: Re-derive from whatever event lastTouchDate/lastTouchDirection actually point at — not from 'the last message that happened to have text'. A calendar acceptance with no text still belongs here, described as that event.

initialReplyLead._note: The lead's chronologically FIRST reply, verbatim, NO prefix — even a one-word 'Sure'. Do not skip a short first reply in favour of a later, meatier message; that also corrupts timeToFirstReplyHrs. Set once.

initialReplySS._note: Our reply TO that first reply — not our original cold email — verbatim, NO prefix. Leave EMPTY if we genuinely have not answered. Empty is a deliberate flag: it drives the digest's reply-owed list and ranks the deal to the top of the Slack stale brief.

timeToFirstReplyHrs._note: Hours from the lead's first reply to OUR reply to it — not their reaction time to our cold email. Blank while initialReplySS is blank.

replyChannel._note: The ACQUISITION channel. Set once; a demo call held later never rewrites this to 'call'.

lemlistCampaignReply._note: Campaign name the reply came from. Blank if the deal has no traceable Lemlist thread.

touchTracking._prefixRule_note: The Client:/SwimScore: prefix belongs on lastMessage ONLY. initialReplyLead and initialReplySS are the literal text with no prefix — the property name already establishes the sender. Found violated on production deals; it is in the end-of-run spot-check for that reason.

sources.lemlist: get_inbox_conversation on the contact — the FULL thread, not the get_inbox_conversations preview. Many Lemlist mailboxes never cc shaffy@ or info@, so zero Gmail results for a Lemlist-sourced lead is a real answer, not a broken search.
sources.front: search_conversations on the contact's email AND domain, then read_conversation on EVERY result — a contact often has 2-3 threads, and the newest updatedAt is not reliably the one with the newest real message. Confirm by content that each thread is that person.
sources.gmail: Search DOMAIN-WIDE — `(from:@theirdomain.com OR to:@theirdomain.com) in:anywhere` — not the single contact address; colleagues at the same clinic correspond too. Fall back to a single address only on a personal domain. in:anywhere already includes Sent. Any SwimScore sender counts as a real outbound touch even when Shaffy is only cc'd: info@myswimscore.com, elara.k@maleswimscore.com, stewart.hill@checkswimscore.com, syb@myswimscore.com, and the rotating campaign aliases.
sources.calendly: ALWAYS also search from:notifications@calendly.com, from:teamcalendly@send.calendly.com, and subject:"Accepted:" — a booking is often the true last touch when no message has moved. Also check DocuSign completion notifications (from:dse@docusign.net or similar) the same way — a signature-completed notification is a real client action.

touchTracking._notificationsAreTouchpoints_warning: Calendly and DocuSign notifications are TOUCHPOINTS, not noise. Found violated in production on 2026-08-19: a run bucketed ~57 Gmail threads as 'system/calendar/billing notification noise' by sender pattern and excluded them from the Step 2 reconciliation without opening them, which meant any Calendly booking or DocuSign signature in that batch never updated its deal's touch-tracking. Every Calendly/DocuSign thread must be individually opened, attributed to a deal (contact email, then company domain), and used to recompute last_touch_date/last_touch_direction/last_message (touchTracking.fields, calendarEventFormat) — never excluded by sender pattern alone. The only sends safe to exclude that way are ones with no client on either end: SwimScore's own internal team calendar invites, Mercury/banking notifications, HubSpot's own system emails, and generic Google account/security notifications.
touchTracking._directionMislabel_warning: BOTH systems lie about direction. Front's kind/origin.kind routinely label SwimScore's own reply-in-thread as inbound-from-customer. Lemlist tags our own outbound as an inbound 'emailsReplied' activity, sometimes with a positive aiLeadInterest score. Read the body and the signature to decide who actually sent a message — never the metadata.
touchTracking._threadTruncation_warning: search_threads SILENTLY TRUNCATES long threads — in production it returned 4 messages of a real 16-message thread, hiding weeks of activity including the actual last touch, with no error or indication. For any thread that looks like a running exchange, call get_thread on the threadId. If it overflows to a saved file, read it with `jq '[.messages[] | {date, sender, toRecipients, ccRecipients, subject, snippet}] | sort_by(.date)'` and take the true last message.
touchTracking._noFabrication_warning: Never write a last_touch_date you have not personally seen in a retrieved thread, activity, or calendar notification. If a date cannot be pinned to a real retrieved item, it is wrong.

replyOwedAudit._note: Added 2026-08-20 at Shaffy's request — this is a KEY metric and goal of this workflow, not a nice-to-have. Steps 1 and 2 only refresh initial_reply_ss for deals they happen to touch (Reply-to-be-enriched, or a thread that landed in the Gmail lookback window) — a deal sitting further along the pipeline with no recent Gmail activity can carry a stale, wrongly-empty initial_reply_ss indefinitely, hiding a reply the team already sent (most replies go out immediately, so an empty field on an older deal is more likely a logging gap than a real gap). This step exists to catch and correct exactly that, pipeline-wide, and to keep the reply-owed list — the thing Shaffy actually acts on — trustworthy.
replyOwedAudit.scope: Every OPEN deal in pipeline 2314112732, i.e. dealstage NOT IN staleFollowUp.excludeStages (Closed Lost, First order placed, Actively ordering, No orders L3M) — not just Reply-to-be-enriched. Includes deals already covered by step 1; re-checking them is redundant but harmless and keeps the logic one rule instead of two.
replyOwedAudit.checkSource: Front ONLY, per Shaffy's instruction — search_conversations on the contact's email AND company domain, then read_conversation on EVERY result (same discipline as touchTracking.sources.front). Front aggregates every rotating cold-outreach mailbox, which is exactly where a same-day reply the team sent would show up even if it never reached Gmail/Lemlist.
replyOwedAudit._ifReplyFound_note: A genuine SwimScore reply-to-the-lead's-first-reply found in Front (verbatim, no prefix, never a placeholder) means the stored empty field was WRONG — this is a correction, not new data being invented. Set initial_reply_ss, recompute time_to_first_reply_hrs from the two real timestamps, and refresh last_touch_date/last_touch_direction/last_message (touchTracking.fields) from whatever the true latest event now is. Attach/update the thread note per the standard note rule (identity line front:<conversationId>) — never skip the note just because this is an audit pass.
replyOwedAudit._ifNoReplyFound_note: No SwimScore reply found in Front → the empty field is correct, not a gap. Leave it exactly as-is (still empty) — this deal genuinely needs a reply and belongs in the reply-owed list. Do not write anything.
replyOwedAudit._noFabrication_note: Never infer a reply happened because 'the team usually replies fast' — that is exactly the assumption this audit exists to verify, not a substitute for checking. Only Front content counts as evidence.
replyOwedAudit.logging: Every deal this step corrects (found a real reply that was missing) gets its own digest line: deal — how long the reply sat unlogged — who replied and when. This log is the actual point of the step: it tells Shaffy who genuinely still needs a reply vs. who was a logging gap already handled, so following up chases the right list.

lemlist._note: Primary source for a lead's first reply, on BOTH channels a campaign runs — email AND LinkedIn. Filter Lemlist's own warm-up traffic: subjects ending '- lemwarmup' are never a real lead.

front._note: Email only, no LinkedIn visibility. Aggregates replies across every rotating cold-outreach sending mailbox (myswimscore.com / withswimscore.com / swimscoreview.com / viewswimscore.com / malescore.com / goswimscore.com). Its real value is catching email follow-ups that never resurface in Lemlist's inbox view. Front ticket status (Open/Waiting/Resolved) and '<name> - In Contact' tags are Front-side handling state — informational only, never mapped onto dealstage. Filter auto-replies: 'Automatic reply:', 'Thank you for your email', 'We will get back to you shortly', 'Thank you for contacted...'.

gmail._note: Narrowed from 2 days to 1 (24h) on 2026-08-20 at Shaffy's request. Every message from the last 24 hours, BOTH directions. Search `in:inbox newer_than:1d` AND `in:sent newer_than:1d` for shaffy@myswimscore.com — a follow-up he sent that has not been answered never appears in the inbox, and missing it produces a false stale flag. Also read threads where he is only cc'd (cc:shaffy@myswimscore.com) and threads from the team senders. MANDATORY RECONCILIATION: count the threads these searches return and count the threads accounted for in the digest (touched, explicitly excluded, or no-matching-deal) — the two must match before the run is reported done. On 2026-08-19, 8 real client threads (NP Modalities, OKC Fertility, Awakin Men's Health, Ares Men's Health, CycleScript, Wellbar Co, Wellness Culture, Perrenia Wellness) matched this exact search and were never logged, while the run's own digest claimed a clean pass — do not repeat that.

shopify._note: Website contact-form submissions ONLY — the 'New customer message' emails to info@myswimscore.com. This is the one inbound channel no automation watches, so it is the one place this workflow creates a deal (see shopifyIntake). Do NOT read Shopify orders or customers — B2C, out of scope for the pipeline entirely.

shopifyIntake._note: The ONLY deal-creation path in this workflow. Keep B2B intent only — a clinic, practice, or partner asking about offering testing to their patients. A patient asking about their own kit, results, or order is B2C: skip, create nothing.
shopifyIntake.searchBeforeCreate: Search by the sender's email on the contact record, by their company domain, AND for any deal linked to that company with no contact. Contact-form leads frequently already exist from an earlier campaign touch — the common case is that a deal is already there.
shopifyIntake._createAt_note: Never any further along the pipeline, however warm the enquiry reads.
shopifyIntake.ownerOnCreate: Omit hubspot_owner_id entirely. HubSpot may auto-populate one anyway — leave whatever it sets (the workflow never sets or clears an owner) and name the new deal in the digest so Shaffy can reassign.
shopifyIntake.thenEnrich: Link the company, attach the enquiry as a note, and set touch-tracking with reply_channel=email, initial_reply_lead = their enquiry text, and initial_reply_ss empty until we have actually answered.

orgLinking._note: Backfill a missing Company on any deal this workflow touches. SEARCH BY DOMAIN FIRST and reuse on match — a blind create produced 5 duplicate companies in one live run. Company records only; never a contact, never a deal (outside shopifyIntake).
orgLinking.matchBy: the deal's associated contact's email domain
orgLinking._personalDomains_note: Never create a company from one of these — flag the deal in the digest for manual review instead.

contactLinking._note: Associate every real participant in a touched thread with that deal, not just the one contact HubSpot happened to attach at creation. A deal is often linked to only the first person who ever replied; a colleague who joins later (a practice manager, another provider) frequently has no association at all, which then hides their messages from a later Front/Gmail domain search. Runs on every deal a run touches, in both step 1 and step 2 — not just intake deals.
contactLinking.matchBy: email address of every distinct external sender/addressee on the thread (skip SwimScore's own addresses)
contactLinking._canCreate_note: SEARCH BY EMAIL FIRST and reuse on match — same discipline as orgLinking, where a blind create produced 5 duplicate companies in one live run. Create a contact only when the email has no record anywhere and it belongs to a real thread participant (firstname/lastname/email pulled from the thread signature, nothing invented); associate it with the deal and, if one exists, the company. Never edit an existing contact's fields — that stays hard rule 3.

staleFollowUp._note: Step 5. A deal is stale when last_touch_date is more than thresholdDays ago. VERIFY DIRECTLY before flagging — an undated from:/to: Gmail search plus Lemlist and Front, reading the actual date of the last message. Never carry a stale flag forward from a stored field or a previous run; that stored field is what is being tested.
staleFollowUp._excludeStages_note: Closed Lost, plus everything from 'First order placed' onward — those are customers, not open pipeline.
staleFollowUp._splitByOwner_note: Group the brief by deal owner: Alex (163314964), then Shaffy (162479602), then Unassigned/other as a third group. Skip a group entirely if empty rather than printing an empty header.
rankWithinGroup: 1. We owe them a reply — initial_reply_ss empty, or last_touch_direction = Inbound. They spoke last and we went quiet. Oldest first.
2. Waiting on them — we spoke last. Oldest first.
staleFollowUp.lineFormat: Deal name, days quiet, who spoke last, and the single most useful detail for picking it back up (what they asked, what was promised).

slack._note: Slack is OUTPUT ONLY in this workflow — the deal channels are no longer read as a source.

_removed_2026-08-19: Removed in the enrichment-only rewrite, deliberately, not by oversight: Notion internal tracker and the notion-todos workflow; Granola call notes; HubSpot Task creation (stale items go to Slack now, not a task queue); reading the Slack deal channels as an ingest source; general deal creation and the newDealDiscovery block (a separate automation creates a deal on every Lemlist reply; only shopifyIntake above still creates); every stage-advance rule; and the owner-clearing policy (it emptied the field the Slack split now groups by).
